name: Eliel
overview: Eliel was a male leader from the tribe of Manasseh, recognized as the head of households within his tribe. His role as a head of households indicates a position of responsibility and authority among the descendants of Manasseh. Scripture records him specifically in 1 Chronicles 5:24.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliel means 'G-d is my G-d,' reflecting a declaration of faith in the true God. This proper name, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 5:24, emphasizes a personal relationship with God, though it was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Eliel is identified as a descendant of Manasseh, linking him genealogically to this prominent Israelite tribe. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide further family relationships for Eliel.
scriptureSignificance: Eliel's significance lies in his leadership role within the tribe of Manasseh, serving as head of households, which denotes his influence and responsibility in organizing and representing his people. His mention in the genealogical records underscores the importance of tribal leadership and continuity in the biblical narrative. Through Eliel, the faithfulness and structure of Israel's tribal system are preserved and highlighted.
